newsitem.title: USA: Black Jesus stirs passions in N.J. community.
newsitem.headline: Black Jesus stirs passions in N.J. community.

text.p: The producers of a Passion play featuring an African-American actor in the role of Jesus Christ contacted the police Tuesday after receiving threats.

The menacing message was left in the voice mail of a staff member at the Park Performing Arts Centre in Union City, New Jersey, a predominantly working-class Hispanic community just across the Hudson River from New York City.

"I'm going to get you," said the mystery caller, who among a litany of profanities made no reference to the black Jesus. But the phone call came in the wake of a growing controversy over the production's non-traditional casting.

Father Kevin Ashe, a Catholic priest who serves as executive director of the performing centre, said the box office had received numerous calls deploring the concept of a black Jesus. Several callers cancelled their reservations in protest.
The theatre, founded by a German Catholic congregation in 1915, staged the first-ever Passion play to be performed in the United States that year; it has housed a Passion production each year since.

The historical drama is being performed every weekend through April 22, in honour of Easter. Passion plays, a dramatic genre dating back to the 13th century, developed from staged readings of Gospel stories about the death and resurrection of Jesus Christ. The earliest surviving play texts are in German.

This year marks the first time a black actor has portrayed Jesus Christ at the arts centre, said Father Ashe. The performer, who goes by the stage name "Dez," appeared in last year's production as Herod. He plays the role on alternate nights, switching off with another, white actor.
